en: The Chapter on Non-Proliferation, Concerning the Question on Inference.
6. The Question on Birth from Karma, etc.

“Venerable Nāgasena, which among these are born of karma (*kammaja*), which are born of cause (*hetuja*), which are born of season (*utuja*), and which are neither born of karma, nor born of cause, nor born of season?
“Whatever beings there are, O Great King, who possess consciousness, they are all born of karma.”
Fire and all types of seeds are born of causes;
earth, mountains, water, and wind—all these are born of the seasons;
space and Nibbāna—these two are not born of karma, not born of causes, and not born of the seasons.
But as for Nibbāna, O Great King, it cannot be said to be born of karma, nor born of cause, nor born of season;
it cannot be said to be arisen, nor unarisen, nor capable of being made to arise; it cannot be said to be past, nor future, nor present;
and it cannot be said to be cognizable by the eye, nor cognizable by the ear, nor cognizable by the nose, nor cognizable by the tongue, nor cognizable by the body.
"Moreover, Great King, Nibbāna is cognizable by the mind, which that noble disciple who is practicing rightly perceives with purified knowledge.

"Delightful, Bhante Nāgasena, is this question! It has been well analyzed, rendered free from doubt, brought to a definitive conclusion, and all uncertainty has been severed. You have resorted to the most excellent among the best of teachers.
The sixth question, concerning that which is born of kamma and so forth, is concluded.
